nodes.name: DW-Ru precursor preparation
nodes.procedure: Initially, 2.5 mmol (0.474 g) of dopamine hydrochloride (DA) was dissolved in 25 mL of water, yielding a 0.1 M solution of dopamine in water. The pH of the dopamine solution was lowered to approximately 2 by adding HCl. Subsequently, RuCl3·xH2O was added to the DA solution and thoroughly stirred. After that, a slow dropwise addition of 25 mL of sodium tungstate solution (containing 2.5 mmol of Na2WO4·2H2O) was performed into the DA-Ru solution. The reaction mixture was stirred for an additional hour, followed by collection of the product (DW-Ru) through centrifugation. The collected product was subsequently washed three times with deionized (DI) water and ethanol. The products were dried overnight at 60°C in an oven to obtain the DW-Ru precursor.

nodes.name: High-temperature carbonization
nodes.procedure: Subsequently, the DW-Ru precursor was subjected to carbonization in an argon furnace at various temperatures (800°C, 900°C, and 1000°C) for 2 h using a ramp rate of 2°C per minute. The final black powder was denoted as Ru/WCx. As a comparison, the effect of Ru content on HER performance was investigated by varying the RuCl3·xH2O (0.025, 0.125, and 0.5 mmol) addition, and the synthesis process was similar to the preparation of Ru/WCx.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images demonstrate that Ru/WCx maintains the morphology of microspheres formed from layered nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images demonstrate that both carbonized pure WCx and Ru/WCx maintain the morphology of microspheres formed from layered nanosheets (Figs. 1b and S3)

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm the microsphere structure formed from layered nanosheets for Ru/WCx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the TEM images further confirm this structure (Figs. 1c and S4a)

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM reveals 2-5 nm Ru/WCx nanoislands distributed over amorphous carbon with lattice spacings of 0.25 nm (WC (100)) and 0.23 nm (WC2 (200)). Brighter spots indicate atomic Ru dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images further reveal 2 - 5 nm Ru/WCx nanoislands distributed over amorphous carbon ... The lattice stripes with the planar spacing of 0.25 nm and 0.23 nm belong to the WC (100) and WC2 (200) crystal planes, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows substantial overlap between Ru and W atom distribution, confirming uniform Ru distribution in WCx nanoislands.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the elemental mapping analysis conducted using energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) showed a substantial overlap between the regions of Ru and W atom distribution in the sample (Fig. 1g)

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Ru/WCx exhibit hexagonal WC (PDF#72-0090) and orthorhombic WC2 (PDF#89-2371) phases with characteristic peaks at 31.5°, 35.6°, 48.3° for WC and 34.4°, 38.0°, 61.7° for WC2. No Ru phase peaks indicate atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD patterns of both WCx and Ru/WCx exhibit similar reflections including hexagonal WC (PDF#72-0090) and orthorhombic WC2 (PDF#89-2371) phases.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show D and G bands at ~1353 and 1589 cm⁻¹ with I_D/I_G ratio of 0.68 for Ru/WCx indicating high graphitization. W-C stretching at 686 and 807 cm⁻¹, W=O at 910 and 955 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectra further verify the presence of the pure WCx and Ru/WCx carbon shells ... The smaller I_D/I_G ratio (0.67 for WCx and 0.68 for Ru/WCx) indicates a higher degree of graphitization

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Ru, W, C, O elements. W 4f_{7/2} spectrum of Ru/WCx is negatively shifted compared to WCx, indicating electron-rich W species.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of the four elements Ru, W, C, and O in the Ru/WCx ... The XPS of W 4 f shows that the W 4 f7/2 spectrum of Ru/WCx is negatively shifted compared to WCx

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP determines Ru content in Ru/WCx as approximately 1.41 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The precise Ru content of Ru/WCx was determined to be approximately 1.41 wt% by using inductively coupled plasma (ICP) atomic emission spectroscopy

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES absorption edge of Ru/WCx is between Ru foil and RuO2, close to RuO2, indicating Ru oxidation after doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The absorption edge of Ru/WCx is located between Ru foil and RuO2, but is very close to that of RuO2, indicating that Ru oxidation occurs after doping with WCx

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows Ru-C peak at 1.72 Å and minor Ru-W peak at 2.23 Å. Coordination number of Ru-C is 6.2, similar to W-C, indicating Ru substitution in WCx lattice.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the main peak of Ru/WCx is centered at 1.72 Å, which is attributed to the scattering characteristics of Ru-C ... a minor Ru-W peak at approximately 2.23 Å ... The coordination number of Ru-C of 6.2 is strikingly similar to that of W-C which is 6

nodes.characterization_summary: N2 sorption BET analysis shows surface areas of 154.2 m²/g for Ru/WCx and 209.6 m²/g for WCx.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nitrogen adsorption analysis showed that both the WCx and Ru/WCx catalysts exhibited good adsorption, and BET analysis displayed surface areas of 209.6 m²/g and 154.2 m²/g, respectively (Fig. S5)

nodes.characterization_summary: TGA under N2 flow reveals substantial weight loss at approximately 400°C and 800°C for DW-Ru precursor, with no additional weight loss beyond 900°C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) conducted under N2 flow revealed substantial weight loss at approximately 400°C and 800°C, with no additional weight loss observed beyond 900°C (Fig. S2)
